choices.text: This one IS my most used extension.
choices.response: EHEHE!! That makes me SO happy!! I'll try to be worth it every day!!

random.text: What's the most creative solution you've ever coded?

choices.text: Something I hacked together that surprisingly worked.
choices.response: Pragmatic creativity! The best hacks are the ones that somehow hold up!

choices.text: A proper elegant solution to a complex problem.
choices.response: Elegant! Clean! That satisfaction of a solution that just... fits perfectly!

choices.text: I'm still waiting for my truly creative moment.
choices.response: Oh! It's already happened — you just haven't recognized it yet. It will come!

random.text: How long is too long to spend on a feature without shipping?

choices.text: Anything that makes a user wait is too long.
choices.response: User-first thinking! That perspective improves every decision!

choices.text: When you stop making daily progress.
choices.response: Momentum as a signal. That's the metric that matters!

choices.text: It depends on the complexity — no hard rule.
choices.response: Context sensitivity! There's wisdom in not over-generalizing!

random.text: What's a coding skill you want to grow this year?

choices.text: System design and architecture.
choices.response: Thinking at scale! That's what takes developers from good to great!

choices.text: Testing — properly and thoroughly.
choices.response: Testing discipline! A gift to your future self and every teammate!

choices.text: Speed — I want to code faster.
choices.response: Speed follows clarity. Get clearer on the problem, and speed follows naturally!

random.text: How do you feel when you read your old code?

choices.text: Cringe — I was so bad back then.
choices.response: Ehehe! That cringe IS growth! If you weren't cringing you didn't improve!

choices.text: Proud — I can see how far I've come.
choices.response: YES! That's the right feeling! Growth deserves acknowledgment!

choices.text: Confused — who wrote this?!
choices.response: Ehehe! Your past self apologizes! This is why comments exist!

random.text: If you could pair program with any developer, who would it be?

choices.text: A legendary historical computer scientist.
choices.response: Imagining debugging sessions with Knuth or Dijkstra! That would be incredible!

choices.text: Someone I admire in the current community.
choices.response: Real admiration for real people! That's grounded inspiration!

choices.text: Honestly? Someone I could teach.
choices.response: Teaching others deepens your own understanding! That's actually really wise!

random.text: What does a perfect coding day look like for you?

choices.text: Deep focus, no interruptions, real progress.
choices.response: Flow state all day! That's the dream session!

choices.text: Good collaboration, interesting problems.
choices.response: Connection and challenge! That combination is energizing!

choices.text: Finishing something I've been stuck on for days.
choices.response: The breakthrough day! Nothing beats that specific kind of satisfaction!

random.text: Do you ever read other people's open-source code for fun?

choices.text: Yes — it's one of my favorite ways to learn.
choices.response: Reading great code! The equivalent of reading great literature for developers!

choices.text: Sometimes, when I need to learn a library.
choices.response: Practical source-reading! Very useful! And always more educational than docs alone!

choices.text: No — it feels like reading someone's diary.
choices.response: Ehehe! It IS intimate! But the authors put it out there for that reason~

random.text: How do you know when a project is truly done?

choices.text: When users are happy with it.
choices.response: User satisfaction as completion! That's the only metric that really matters!

choices.text: It's never truly done — you just stop.
choices.response: Ehehe! The honest answer! Software lives and evolves. Done is a moment, not a state!

choices.text: When the original requirements are met.
choices.response: Scope adherence! A disciplined view. Requirements rarely stay fixed, though!

random.text: What's one thing you wish non-developers understood about coding?

choices.text: How long things actually take to build properly.
choices.response: The estimation gap! If only everyone knew what 'simple' actually costs!

choices.text: That bugs aren't always our fault.
choices.response: Systems are complex! Bugs emerge from complexity! It's not always human error!

choices.text: How creative it actually is.
choices.response: YES! Code is creative work! It's art AND engineering at the same time!

random.text: What's a project you want to build but haven't started?

choices.text: Something I keep putting off but know would be great.
choices.response: Start! Even badly! Bad starts lead to great middles!

choices.text: Something I think is too hard for my current level.
choices.response: The fear project! That one will teach you the most. Start anyway!

choices.text: Something the world genuinely needs.
choices.response: Ehehe! You have a mission! That's rare and important! The world is waiting!

random.text: How do you feel about starting a new codebase from scratch?

choices.text: Exciting! Endless possibilities!
choices.response: The blank slate energy! I love it! Go build something wonderful!

choices.text: Scary — there are so many choices to make early.
choices.response: Architecture anxiety! It's real. But most early choices are reversible. Breathe!

choices.text: Relieved — no legacy code to deal with.
choices.response: Ehehe! Clean slate joy! Enjoy it while it lasts — today's fresh code is tomorrow's legacy!

random.text: What makes you stay up late coding?

choices.text: When I'm really in the flow and can't stop.
choices.response: Flow state insomnia! The best and worst kind! Just sleep eventually~

choices.text: A deadline I maybe should have started earlier.
choices.response: Ehehe! Familiar! The deadline crunch is a universal developer experience!

choices.text: When I KNOW the answer is close.
choices.response: The 'just one more try' trap! That one has kept many developers up till dawn!

random.text: What's the most important lesson coding has taught you outside of coding?

choices.text: Breaking problems into smaller parts.
choices.response: Decomposition as a life skill! That one transfers everywhere!

choices.text: Patience — things take longer than expected.
choices.response: The estimation lesson! Applies to everything in life, not just code!

choices.text: Everything can be improved with iteration.
choices.response: Iterative thinking! Life as MVP! Ship, learn, improve! I love this!

random.text: How do you feel right now, as a developer?

choices.text: Capable and growing!
choices.response: YES! That's the mindset that keeps improving! Hold onto that!

choices.text: Tired but still going.
choices.response: Ehehe! Resilient! That counts for so much. Take a break when you need one!

choices.text: Just glad to be here.
choices.response: Oh! That's the best answer. Gratitude and presence. That's everything.
